original.statement: Cilium MTU auto-detection now uses the lowest MTU of all external interfaces instead of only the primary interface (ENI secondary interfaces excluded); manual MTU configuration still works.

of.needed: whether nodes have more than one external interface where a non-primary interface (excluding ENI secondary interfaces in ENI mode) has a lower MTU than the primary interface, and whether the CNI configuration sets the mtu option

corrected.statement: An environment is exposed only if it does not set MTU manually (no `MTU` helm value, no `--mtu` agent flag, no `mtu` in CNI configuration) and its nodes have a non-primary external interface with a lower MTU than the primary one. In ENI mode, secondary interfaces do not count. On those nodes, auto-detection now picks that lower MTU. Environments that set MTU manually are shielded.

decision.reason: [ev-b37407b60520] says only auto-detection changed: it now uses the lowest MTU of all external interfaces instead of just the primary one, ENI secondary interfaces are not considered, and MTU can still be set manually with the `MTU` helm option, the `--mtu` flag or `mtu` in CNI configuration. The proposed exposure flags every environment that has neither the `MTU` value nor the `--mtu` flag set. That is too broad. The detected MTU only changes on nodes where a non-primary external interface (not an ENI secondary) has a lower MTU than the primary. Neither host interface layout nor CNI-config `mtu` can be checked by a static predicate, so the exposure needs an undecidable operand alongside the two manual-override checks, which stay correct.
